Ack.description: The result of a method that only acknowledges: an empty map.

AgentPreset.description: A provider-owned agent composition (DeepSeek Harness presets).

AppThread.description: A user-visible conversation. It survives provider exits.

deletedAt.description: Soft delete; cleanup runs as effects.

modelSelection.description: The default for the next run.

worktreeOwned.description: Created by Waku, so deleting the thread removes it.

callbacks_are_live_only.description: The reply must reach the same live process. A restart loses the request.

ArchivedPage.description: Archived threads, most recently archived first.

limit.description: At most [`MAX_ARCHIVED_PAGE`]; that is also the default.

Attachment.description:
A file attached to a message. Mirrors `model::MessageAttachment` with
camelCase field names.

mention.description: Provider-facing path text, relative to the workspace when possible.

path.description: Absolute path on the daemon host, handed to the provider.

AttachmentsImportParams.description:
`attachments.import` params: an attachment assembled from uploaded
blobs. A file attachment has one part (its `relativePath` is ignored); a
directory has one part per file.

AttachmentsImportPathParams.description:
`attachments.importPath` params: copy a file or directory on the daemon
host into the attachment store.

path.description: With a `waku-attachment:` reference, the file inside it.

localPath.description:
Where the file is on the daemon host; only on the local socket, where
the client may read it directly.

BlobsPutParams.description:
`blobs.put` params. `channel` must not be in use by a subscription or
another upload; it is free again once the reply arrives.

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex. Verified when given, and lets the daemon answer at once
for a blob it already holds (`deduplicated`); the client then stops
and sends an empty DATA frame with `FIN`.

size.description: Exactly the bytes that follow, at most `maxBlobBytes`.

BlobsStatParams.description:
`blobs.stat` params: a `waku-blob:` reference, or a
`waku-attachment:` reference with the `path` of a file inside it.

gitRef.description:
New refs: `refs/waku/t/<thread>/<scope>/<ordinal>`; imported refs keep
their names.

CheckpointFile.description: One file of a checkpoint diff summary.

CleanupReason.description:
Why a worktree was removed, kept, or could not be removed. Clients
localize these; `base` names the branch compared with.

instanceId.description: Stable per installation, so a reconnect is recognized.

oneOf.description: The whole retained output; `truncated` when some of it was dropped.
New output after the previous frame.
The command finished; the stream ends after this.

itemId.description: A command execution turn item (or a background node's item).

CommitSnapshot.description: What a commit dialog shows before committing.

ComposerDrafts.description:
Unsent composer text, per project (a thread not started yet) and per
thread.

instanceId.description:
The provider instance whose commands are listed. Required until a
thread's own instance can stand in for it.

root.description: The project the commands are discovered in.

ComputerUsePermissionsParams.description:
`computerUse.permissions` params. `prompt: true` asks macOS to show its
permission prompts; it needs `operate` and the local socket.

column.description: 1-based, in characters (Unicode scalar values) of the line.

ContextRecord.description:
A composer context record (a file, a selection, a terminal excerpt…).
The record body is opaque to the orchestrator.

ContextUsage.description: How full the provider's context window is.

oneOf.description: The daemon's local token (`run/local.token`).
A session token issued by pairing.

A one-time pairing secret; `welcome.issuedCredential` returns the
session token.

defaultCwd.description: Where a thread without a project runs by default.

projectlessRoot.description: The folder scratch projects are created in.

DaemonShutdownParams.description: `daemon.shutdown` params. Only a desktop-owned daemon accepts it.

DelegatedCompletionCohort.description: (P3) The delegated-task completion cohort of a parent run.

Directory.description: A directory on the daemon host, for project pickers.

DispatchCommand.description:
A client command (RFC 0001 "Commands", dotted tags). A command this
daemon does not know — or a daemon-internal one — does not decode, and
the call is answered `badRequest`.

The union is closed (`x-waku-closed` in the schema) because only clients
send it: the daemon is the side that must refuse what it does not know.

oneOf.description: Policy picks inside the thread lock: start, steer or queue.
Prepare a worktree first, then start.

DispatchParams.description:
`orchestration.dispatch` params. Idempotent by `commandId`: a retry with
the same id returns the first outcome.

duplicate.description: The command id was already dispatched; nothing new happened.

sequence.description:
The command's last committed sequence. On the dispatching connection,
every event up to it is queued on subscribed streams before this
reply.

DomainEvent.description:
A committed domain fact. Internally tagged by `type` (RFC 0003 §1.1) so an
unknown event type skips its payload and decodes to `Unknown`.

oneOf.description: An event type written by a newer version.

mention.description: The `@` mention text in the draft.

DraftChange.description:
Set one draft, or remove it with `draft` absent (an empty draft is a
removal too).

DraftTarget.description: Which draft a change applies to.

oneOf.description: The composer of a project's next thread.

DraftsApplyParams.description:
`drafts.apply` params. Changes are keyed, so concurrent clients only
conflict on the same draft; `baseRevision` makes the whole apply
conditional (`conflict` with `revisionConflict` otherwise).

DraftsItem.description:
`drafts` items: a snapshot (skipped when `after` is the current
revision), `synchronized`, then the changes of every apply.

DraftsSnapshot.description:
`drafts.get` result. `revision` is a content hash: compare for equality
only.

End.description: The last message of a subscription. Its channel may be reused afterwards.

resumeAfter.description: The last cursor delivered, to resubscribe from (after `overflow`).

oneOf.description:
The subscription's live budget overflowed; resubscribe from
`resumeAfter`. Other streams on the connection are unaffected.
A newer subscription of the same client replaced this one.

storeId.description:
The event store's id (RFC 0001); cursors from another store are
answered with a snapshot.

message.description: English, for logs. Clients localize by `code`.

ErrorDetails.description: Typed detail for an [`Error`]; an open union.

oneOf.description:
`files.write`, `settings.update` and `drafts.apply` against a stale
base revision.
RFC 0002 `Unsupported`.
The limit that `payloadTooLarge` or `busy` hit.

blob.description: A blob reference to download the content from, otherwise.

revision.description: A content hash, the base revision for a later `files.write`.

text.description: The content, when it is text and small enough to send inline.

FileEntry.description: A file or directory (with a trailing `/`) relative to the root.

FileRevision.description: The revision a file has after `files.write`.

maxBytes.description: Refuse files larger than this instead of reading them.

regex.description:
`query` is a regular expression (Rust `regex` syntax) instead of a
literal.

FilesSearchEntriesParams.description:
`files.searchEntries` params: the project's files and directories for
`@` mentions, fuzzy-ranked by `query` (all of them, shallow first, when it
is empty).

expanded.description: Directories (relative to `root`) whose children are listed too.

FindSnippet.description: A match of the navigation window, with its snippet.

FsBrowseParams.description:
`fs.browse` params: an absolute daemon-host directory, or the home
directory when absent.

GitStatusFile.description: One changed path, with git's porcelain status letters.

compression.description: Compression the client accepts for the daemon → client direction.

maxMessageBytes.description:
The client's receive cap; the daemon uses the smaller of its own and
this.

HistoryPage.description:
Older turn items, bounded like the snapshot window, with the runs they
belong to. `next` continues further back.

InstanceParams.description: The params of a read about one provider instance.

ItemsAround.description:
How many turn items `threads.find` loads before and after the current
match, each at most [`MAX_FIND_ITEMS_AROUND`].

JsonText.description:
Opaque JSON text, never parsed by the protocol layer (RFC 0003 §5.1).
Replaces `serde_json::Value` wherever provider-native JSON is carried.

Limits.description: The limits in force for the rest of the connection.

displayText.description: What the user typed, before attachment mentions.

ModelSelection.description: The provider, model and per-model options of a thread or run.

resumeCursor.description:
The driver's opaque resume cursor (today's `ProviderResumeCursor`,
serialized), kept for native resume (R23).

NoParams.description: The params of a method that takes none: an empty map.

NodeId.description: Also a `Subagent`'s id, as in T3.

Notification.description: A background-work notification carried by a message or a turn item.

NotificationSource.description:
Where a background-work notification came from. As in T3, an unknown
source decodes as `BackgroundTask` (RFC 0001 "Turn items").

PermissionOption.description:
One option of an approval request. `id` is the provider's own option id,
kept through normalization (RFC 0002).

PlanKind.description: The variant part of a [`Plan`], nested under `kind` (R22).

ProviderFailure.description: A normalized provider or preparation failure.

code.description: At most 128 bytes; `"process_loss"` after a daemon crash.

message.description: At most 4096 bytes, redacted by the producer.

ProviderInstanceId.description:
A configured provider instance. Phase 2: the driver tag (`"codex"`);
Phase 3: `"codex:<name>"`.

contextWindows.description: Context window sizes offered as a per-session choice.

ProviderRef.description:
A provider-native id with its strength. App ids are primary; this is a
reference only.

fingerprint.description: Fallback correlation only; never full assistant text.

ProviderSessionSummary.description:
A provider-native conversation a thread can be imported from
(`threadImport`).

cwd.description: Where the conversation ran, on the daemon host.

nativeId.description: The provider's id for the conversation.

resumeCursor.description: The driver's opaque resume cursor, passed back unchanged.

ProviderSessionsListParams.description:
`providerSessions.list` params: one provider's resumable CLI
conversations on the daemon host, newest first, without those already
imported. Only the chosen provider's CLI is asked.

limit.description: At most [`MAX_PROVIDER_SESSIONS`], which is also the default.

ProviderStatus.description: A provider instance as the providers list shows it.

installed.description: Whether the binary was found, once a probe has run.

planUsage.description: Whether this provider reports plan usage (`providers.planUsage`).

version.description: The CLI version, once a probe asked for it.

ownerNodeId.description: Set for a subagent's provider thread.

runAttemptId.description: A Codex `/goal` keeps one attempt across several turns.

ProvidersItem.description:
`providers` items. Statuses change when settings enable, disable or
re-point a provider and when a probe runs; plan usage when
`providers.planUsage` fetches it.

refresh.description: Ask the CLI for a fresh catalog instead of the cached one.

discoverModels.description: Ask the CLI for its model catalog (slow; spawns the provider).

probeVersion.description: Ask the CLI for its version.

Rejected.description:
The daemon's answer to a refused `hello`. Everything the client pipelined
after `hello` is discarded.

ResponseCapability.description: How a request can be answered.

oneOf.description: The answer goes to a live provider session.
Answered by a new user message (Codex async questions).

completeContext.description: The patch carries full file context (small diffs only).

patch.description: The unified patch; a blob reference above [`MAX_INLINE_PATCH_BYTES`].

ReviewDiffSource.description:
Which changes `review.diff` compares. The last turn of a thread is
`threads.turnDiff`.

oneOf.description: Working tree and index against `HEAD`, untracked files included.
Working tree against the index.
Index against `HEAD`.
Commits on the branch since it left its base.
Everything on the branch since its base, committed or not.

RootOpParams.description: The params of a mutation that only names a root (`vcs.push`, `vcs.pull`).

RootParams.description: The params of a read that only names a root.

RootRef.description: Where a files, vcs or terminal call operates.

oneOf.description:
The thread's worktree, or its project's root, as the orchestrator
records them.
An absolute path on the daemon host.

Run.description: A counted, user-visible turn. Only its root node completes it.

providerCompletedAt.description: Provider terminal; the duration excludes finalization.

nativeThreadId.description: The input destination, kept when provider-thread rows are reused.

RunContinuation.description: How a run continues an earlier one.

RunOrdinalRange.description: An inclusive range of app run ordinals.

supported_modes.description:
Modes the provider enforces itself. A stored mode outside this set runs
as `RuntimeMode::Ask`, as in T3's `RuntimePolicy.ts`.

RuntimeResponse.description: A user's answer to a runtime request.

oneOf.description: `option_id` is the provider's own option id, exactly as emitted.

Settings.description: The daemon's settings as clients see them.

continueThreadsAfterRestart.description:
Continue threads whose turn a daemon restart interrupted (#59). On
by default.

disabledProviders.description: Provider instance ids that are switched off.

providerBinaryOverrides.description: Binary path per provider instance id.

storage.description: The managed worktree folder and its cleanup rules.

oneOf.description: Everything up to `cursor` has been delivered: data is fresh.

SettingsPatch.description:
The settings fields to change. Touching `disabledProviders` or
`providerBinaryOverrides` needs `providers:manage` as well.

continueThreadsAfterRestart.description: Continue threads whose turn a daemon restart interrupted (#59).

providerBinaryOverrides.description: The whole map: binary path per provider instance id.

storage.description:
The managed worktree folder and its cleanup rules. Moving the folder
keeps the old location in `previousWorktreesDirectories`.

revision.description: Equal revisions mean equal settings; compare for equality only.

SettingsUpdateParams.description:
`settings.update` params. Fields present in `patch` replace the current
value; with `baseRevision`, the update is refused with `conflict`
(`revisionConflict`) unless the settings still have that revision.

oneOf.description:
Rows at `cursor`. A snapshot over [`SHELL_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`] is split;
only the last part has `complete`.

The row changed; `location` is where it is now, so a client drops a
row that left the location it subscribed to.
Everything up to `cursor` has been delivered.

Skill.description: One skill, merged across the places it is installed.

installs.description: The first install is the primary one.

project.description: The project's name, for project skills.

rowKey.description: A stable key for list rows (53 bits).

dir.description: The skill directory on the daemon host.

source.description:
`shared` (`~/.agents/skills` and the like) or the provider id whose
folder holds it.

SkillsListParams.description: `skills.list` params: user skills plus those of these projects.

SkillsTrashParams.description: `skills.trash` params: move skill directories to the trash.

template.description: The prompt template a Waku command expands to.

StorageSettings.description: The managed worktree folder and its cleanup rules (#62).

previousWorktreesDirectories.description: Earlier locations, still managed by cleanup.

worktreesDirectory.description:
Where new worktrees are created; the daemon's default folder when
absent. Absolute; a leading `~` is expanded.

path.description: The materialized file or directory on the daemon host.

StreamCursor.description:
Where a subscriber stands in a stream. A client passes its last *applied*
cursor as `subscribe.after`; the daemon decides between replay and a
snapshot.

oneOf.description: The global event sequence of event store `store` (shell, thread).

A revision of a small document (settings, providers, access, drafts).
Revisions are compared for equality only.
A byte offset into `generation` (terminal output, blob download).

StreamSpec.description: What a `subscribe` asks for: an open union tagged by stream name.

oneOf.description:
`snapshot`, then `updated` on every change; `synchronized` after the
snapshot (or alone when `after` is the current revision).

`meta`, then the blob's bytes as DATA within the credit window with
`FIN` on the last chunk, then `end{completed}`.

Navigation rows: a snapshot (or the deltas since `after`), then
`synchronized`, then a delta per changed row.

One thread: a bounded snapshot or the replayed gap, `synchronized`,
then its events and live `delta`s.
The live output of one command, while its row is expanded.
Composer drafts: a snapshot, `synchronized`, then every change.
Provider statuses and plan usage.

One terminal: `attached`, then output as DATA under credit; input as
DATA from the client when `interactive` (which needs `terminal`).
The open terminals.
A repository's status while subscribed, at most once a second.

A stream this build does not know; answered with
`end{error: unsupported}`.

after.description: The client's last applied cursor, to resume from.

channel.description:
Chosen by the client, unique among its open subscriptions; `0` is
reserved.

window.description: Initial DATA credit in bytes, for streams that carry DATA.

cwd.description: The shell's working directory on the daemon host.

TerminalItem.description:
`terminal` items. The stream starts with `attached`; then output arrives
as DATA, the first `replay` bytes of it being the retained tail that ends
at `offset`. A client's cursor is `offset{generation, offset + live
bytes received after the replay}`; resuming from it gets only the output
it missed when that is still retained, else a fresh tail.

offset.description: The raw output offset the replay ends at; live output follows.

replay.description:
How many DATA bytes of retained output follow before live output
(0 when the cursor was current).

truncated.description: Earlier output exists that the replay does not contain.

oneOf.description:
Clear the screen and scrollback: the terminal was cleared, restarted
(a new `generation`), or this subscriber fell behind what the daemon
retains. `replay` DATA bytes of retained output follow, then live
output from `offset`.

The shell exited. The terminal stays open with its output until it is
restarted or closed.

TerminalListSpec.description:
`terminalList` spec: every terminal, or those whose working directory is
`root`.

TerminalSpec.description:
`terminal` spec. `interactive` (which needs the `terminal` scope) makes
DATA the client sends on the channel the terminal's input.

TextPayload.description:
Text that may be too large for a message (RFC 0003 §1.1 `Payload<T>`):
inline, or a blob reference to download.

ThreadFindParams.description:
`threads.find` params: every match of `query` inside one thread, loaded
by any client or not.

anchor.description:
The position the reader is at: the current match is the first at or
after it. Absent: the latest match.

itemsAround.description:
Also load the turn items around the current match, so a client can
jump to history it has not paged in.

window.description:
Snippets around the current match, at most [`MAX_FIND_WINDOW`]; 17
when absent.

current.description: The current match, as an index into `matches`.

items.description:
With `itemsAround`: the turn items around the current match,
wire-projected, ascending by `position`.

matches.description: Every match in transcript order (at most 5,000).

oneOf.description:
A committed event of the thread, wire-projected. Apply as an upsert
by entity id; `seq` is the stream cursor.

Live text, never sequenced, persisted or replayed. Apply only when
`rev` is the item's `streamRev + 1`, then increment `streamRev`; on a
gap ignore deltas until the next snapshot of the item.
The snapshot or replay is complete; data is fresh up to `cursor`.

ThreadProjection.description:
The part of a thread a client holds: the thread, the control rows of the
runs in view and of every non-terminal run, the always-required control
records (pending runtime requests and their rows), and a bounded window of
wire-projected turn items in position order. Events apply to it as
upserts by entity id.

messages.description:
Messages of non-terminal runs (queued ones included); with
`compactTurnItems`, only those no turn item in the window shows.

ThreadRow.description:
One navigation row: the thread (never its transcript) and its derived
sidebar state.

ThreadSearchHit.description:
One thread found by `threads.search`: its best match (the title, else
the latest matching message, else the latest matching plan). Results are
ordered by that source, then by recency.

activityAt.description: The thread's last reply, else its last update (epoch milliseconds).

entityId.description: The message, plan or thread id that matched.

position.description: The matching turn item's position; absent for a title match.

ThreadSearchParams.description:
`threads.search` params: threads across projects whose title, messages
or plans hold every word of `query` (as prefixes).

ThreadSnapshot.description:
A bounded thread snapshot: the `thread` stream's first item and the
`threads.snapshot` result.

budgetExceeded.description:
The window was cut by its byte budget rather than by its turn or item
count.

cursor.description: The event-store position the snapshot reflects.

compactTurnItems.description: Leave out messages a turn item in the snapshot already shows.

TokenUsage.description: Token accounting as the provider reports it.

ToolIcon.description: An icon for a tool's activity row.

nonExecutionKind.description: Open string, e.g. `"read"` for a tool that only looks.

ToolSource.description: The integration a tool belongs to (an MCP server, the browser, …).

TreeEntry.description: One row of the file tree, depth first.

active_steering_interrupts_tools.description: Native steering cancels pending tools before consuming the message.

TurnItem.description: One display row of a thread.

kind.description: The variant, nested rather than flattened (R22).

position.description:
`(run_ordinal << 24) | n`, assigned once by `decide` (R15). Doubles as
the history-paging cursor.

streamRev.description: The number of live `delta`s folded into this snapshot (RFC 0003 §5.4).

bodyOmitted.description: Wire projection only (#57); never set in storage.

outputTruncated.description: Set in storage when the 256 KiB cap applied (R12).

oneOf.description:
A kind written by a newer version. Clients skip the row and still
advance their cursor.

UsageHistory.description: Token and cost history read from the providers' local logs.

projectIds.description: Projects whose usage is broken out per project.

firstDay.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, the first day of the month.

UsageProviderPart.description: One provider's part of a day, month or project.

UsageProviderSlice.description: One provider's share of a window. `provider` is a provider id.

oneOf.description: The last `days` days, today included.
The last `months` calendar months, this one included.

baseRef.description:
Branch or commit to start from; the repository's default branch when
absent.

branchHint.description:
Text the branch and folder names are derived from (a prompt or a
title).

threadId.description:
The thread the worktree is for, recorded in its name; a fresh id when
absent.

VcsGenerateCommitMessageParams.description:
`vcs.generateCommitMessage` params. The provider instance's binary comes
from settings, never from the request.

VcsRemoveWorktreeParams.description:
`vcs.removeWorktree` params. Without `force`, git refuses a worktree
with modified or untracked files.

path.description: Absolute path of a linked worktree.

VcsStatusItem.description:
`vcsStatus` items: the status whenever it changes, at most once per
[`VCS_STATUS_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`]. Each replaces the previous one.

at.description: When it was read, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

VcsSwitchRefParams.description:
`vcs.switchRef` params: check out `name`, creating it first with
`create`.

Welcome.description: The daemon's answer to an accepted `hello`.

WorkspaceStrategy.description: Where a thread's next run works.

branchDeleted.description: The `waku/` branch was deleted with the worktree.

omitted.description: Rows beyond the report's bound, counted but not listed.

WorktreeCleanupSettings.description: Automatic worktree cleanup rules; all off by default.

deletedTasks.description: Remove the worktree of a deleted thread.

finishedAfterDays.description: Remove a worktree this many days after its threads finished.

inactiveAfterDays.description: Remove a worktree whose threads had no activity for this many days.

merged.description: Remove a worktree whose branch was merged into its base.

removeUnpushedCommits.description:
Allow removing a worktree whose branch holds commits that exist
nowhere else (the branch is kept).

unchanged.description: Remove a worktree with no commits beyond its base.

nextRunAt.description: When the next automatic run is due, if any rule is enabled.
